flawed_step: The key inductive step fails: 'a maximum-degree vertex always belongs to some minimum vertex cover of the remaining graph'. When degrees tie, greedy may pick a vertex that is in no minimum cover.
counterexample: Path P5: vertices a-b-c-d-e, edges ab, bc, cd, de. Degrees a=1, b=2, c=2, d=2, e=1. The minimum vertex cover is {b,d}, size 2. It cannot be 1 because ab and de are disjoint. Legal greedy run: pick c (degree 2 = max), which leaves edges ab and de. Pick b (degree 1 = max), which leaves de. Pick d. The output {c,b,d} has size 3 > 2.
assessment_summary: False. On the path P5, greedy can break the degree tie by picking the center vertex c, then needs two more vertices, giving size 3. The minimum cover {b,d} has size 2.
